examples.name: 00-first-scene
examples.title: First scene
examples.summary: First scene: a formula writes on, its graph draws on a pair of axes, and a three-qubit circuit builds column by column.

examples.name: 01-shapes
examples.title: Shapes
examples.summary: Any path morphs into any other: the engine aligns their points, so a circle can become a square, a hexagon, and a star without a seam.

examples.name: 04-fourier-epicycles
examples.title: Fourier epicycles
examples.summary: The outline of an integral sign, traced by eighty rotating arrows.

examples.name: 05-riemann-sums
examples.title: Riemann sums
examples.summary: Left Riemann sums with 4, 8, 16, and 64 rectangles close in on the integral.

examples.name: 06-polar-roses
examples.title: Polar roses
examples.summary: Roses r = cos(k theta): k petals for odd k, 2k for even k, and a fractional k needs more than one turn to close.

examples.name: 07-phase-portrait
examples.title: Phase portrait
examples.summary: The damped pendulum: arrows show the flow, streamlines follow it, and one trajectory spirals into the resting state.

examples.name: 08-roots-of-unity
examples.title: Roots of unity
examples.summary: The seven solutions of z^7 = 1 sit evenly on the unit circle, and multiplying by the first root turns the whole set onto itself.

examples.name: 09-taylor-series
examples.title: Taylor series
examples.summary: Partial sums of the sine series hug the curve over a wider and wider stretch as terms are added.

examples.name: 10-central-limit
examples.title: Central limit
examples.summary: The average of more dice looks more and more like a bell curve.

examples.name: 11-derivative
examples.title: Derivative
examples.summary: Generated from one expression by the math engine.

examples.name: 12-definite-integral
examples.title: Definite integral
examples.summary: Generated from one expression by the math engine.

examples.name: 13-matrix-product
examples.title: Matrix product
examples.summary: Generated from one expression by the math engine.

examples.name: 14-eigenvectors-solved
examples.title: Eigenvectors solved
examples.summary: Generated from one expression by the math engine.

examples.name: 15-gradient-descent
examples.title: Gradient descent
examples.summary: A tilted valley: gradient descent zigzags across the narrow direction while it creeps along the long one.

examples.name: 16-eigenvectors
examples.title: Eigenvectors
examples.summary: Most vectors get knocked off their span; eigenvectors only stretch.

examples.name: 17-linear-transformation
examples.title: Linear transformation
examples.summary: A shear, then a quarter turn.

examples.name: 18-quadratic
examples.title: Quadratic
examples.summary: Generated from one expression by the math engine.

examples.name: 19-typography
examples.title: Typography
examples.summary: Text and TeX are both outlines, so letters can travel: an anagram rearranges itself, each letter flying to its new place.

examples.name: 20-grover-explainer
examples.title: Grover explainer
examples.summary: Narrated Grover search for 110, generated entirely from the program.

examples.name: 21-qft-explainer
examples.title: QFT explainer
examples.summary: Narrated quantum Fourier transform of the basis state 22 on five qubits.

examples.name: 22-bell-state
examples.title: Bell state
examples.summary: A Bell pair: one Hadamard, one controlled X, then both qubits measured.

examples.name: 23-ghz-state
examples.title: GHZ state
examples.summary: Three-qubit GHZ state: the Bell construction extended down a ladder.

examples.name: 24-teleportation
examples.title: Teleportation
examples.summary: Teleporting a prepared state from qubit 0 to qubit 2.

examples.name: 25-bernstein-vazirani
examples.title: Bernstein vazirani
examples.summary: Bernstein-Vazirani reads a hidden bitstring with a single query.

examples.name: 26-phase-estimation
examples.title: Phase estimation
examples.summary: Phase estimation of P(3 pi / 4) with three counting qubits.

examples.name: 30-pythagoras-boards
examples.title: Pythagoras boards
examples.summary: The rearrangement proof: four copies of a right triangle inside a square of side a + b leave c^2 uncovered, and after sliding them, a^2 + b^2.

examples.name: 31-blueprint-construction
examples.title: Blueprint construction
examples.summary: Euclid, Elements I.1: an equilateral triangle on a given segment, with nothing but a compass and a straightedge.

examples.name: 32-paper-notes
examples.title: Paper notes
examples.summary: Study notes on ruled paper: the derivative as a limit of secant slopes, drawn and annotated by hand.

examples.name: 40-platonic-solids
examples.title: Platonic solids
examples.summary: The five Platonic solids, turning in place under key, fill, and rim light.

examples.name: 41-surface-plot
examples.title: Surface plot
examples.summary: A surface drawn in along x, then seen from a slowly turning camera.

examples.name: 42-bloch-gates
examples.title: Bloch gates
examples.summary: Each single-qubit gate is a rotation of the Bloch sphere.

examples.name: 43-qsphere
examples.title: Qsphere
examples.summary: The Q-sphere of a three-qubit state: basis states sit by Hamming weight from |000> at the north pole to |111> at the south; dot size is the amplitude and color the phase.

examples.name: 44-cross-section
examples.title: Cross section
examples.summary: A trefoil knot turning in place beside a torus that a plane slices open, showing the circular cross-section of its tube.

examples.name: 45-printable-circuit
examples.title: Printable circuit
examples.summary: A Qubi program as a physical object: the same model exports to STL or 3MF for a printer (qgfx render ... --format stl).

examples.name: 50-images
examples.title: Images
examples.summary: One picture used three ways: as an object that moves and scales, as a texture on a plane in 3D, and as a dimmed background for the whole frame.

examples.name: 51-benford
examples.title: Benford
examples.summary: Leading digits of 2^1 ... 2^1000, counted exactly with BigInt, against Benford's law log10(1 + 1/d).

examples.name: 52-dijkstra
examples.title: Dijkstra
examples.summary: Dijkstra's algorithm settles the nearest unsettled node, then relaxes its edges.

examples.name: 53-insertion-sort
examples.title: Insertion sort
examples.summary: Insertion sort: each new bar slides left past every taller bar before it.

examples.name: 54-markov-chain
examples.title: Markov chain
examples.summary: A three-state weather chain.

examples.name: 55-pendulum
examples.title: Pendulum
examples.summary: A damped pendulum swings on the left while its angle is traced against time on the right.

examples.name: 56-conformal-map
examples.title: Conformal map
examples.summary: The grid of the right half-plane pushed through z -> z^2: straight lines become parabolas, and every crossing stays a right angle.

examples.name: 57-composition
examples.title: Composition
examples.summary: Scenes compose: two gallery scenes play side by side, each inside its own scaled group, on one shared timeline.

examples.name: 58-palette-helper
examples.title: Palette helper
examples.summary: A theme from a few words: the palette helper picks a background, ink, and two accents from a hue and a mood.
